newsitem.title: USA: Homes, schools evacuated in NY pipeline scare.
newsitem.headline: Homes, schools evacuated in NY pipeline scare.

text.p: Homes and schools were evacuated for hours Wednesday as police used a remote-controlled robot to remove a suspected bomb propped up against a natural gas pipeline on Staten Island, officials said.

The robot and a police bomb squad officer took the device away from the pipeline and put it on a protected vehicle for examination at 1:45 p.m. EST, almost five hours after it was first reported to police.

"The device was a cylinder the size of a can, with wires and a power source, but whether it's viable as an explosive device or not is being investigated," a police spokesman, Sgt. Nicholas Breeland said.
A number of schools and homes in the surrounding area were ordered closed and evacuated while police dealt with the potential hazard.

Police said the device had been placed against a natural gas pipeline owned by the Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line (Transco) company that serves Brooklyn Union Gas, forcing the precautionary closure of a jet fuel pipeline alongside it.
Transco said it was repressurizing its natural gas pipeline after reducing the pressure earlier as a precaution.
Buckeye Pipeline Co. has a petroleum products line that carries jet fuel to John F. Kennedy airport running parallel to Transco's pipeline.
Airport operations were not affected, said a spokeswoman for the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, which manages the region's three major airports.
